headline: Tk 500 and 17 mins: NID data being sold online in Bangladesh
summary: An investigation reveals a thriving underground market where sensitive personal data, including NIDs and call records, are sold via Facebook, Telegram, and WhatsApp.
details: An investigation by Dismislab has uncovered an online market where citizens' sensitive personal data is being sold through Facebook advertisements, websites, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

The data available for purchase includes National Identity Cards (NIDs), call detail records (CDRs), mobile phone location data, SMS lists, tax identification numbers (TINs), and passport information.
The report identified 10 active websites and over 600 Facebook advertisements in a single month. Researchers found that NID PDFs were delivered within 17 minutes for a payment of Tk 500.
In another instance, call detail records (CDRs) for a mobile number were provided within two and a half hours after a payment of Tk 1,050, matching the subscriber's actual call history.
Mobile tower-based location data, including a Google Maps link, was also obtained for a payment, delivered within 16 minutes of the payment.
Some sellers claim to use an API to breach government servers to collect this data, though Dismislab could not independently verify this specific claim.
Experts warn that CDRs can be used to track a person's movement patterns and identify who they have been in contact with, posing a significant privacy risk.
caption:
Your NID and call records could be for sale for as little as Tk 500. An investigation reveals a massive data breach market in Bangladesh.

An investigation by Dismislab has uncovered an online market where citizens' sensitive personal data is being sold through Facebook advertisements, websites, Telegram, and WhatsApp.

The data available for purchase includes National Identity Cards (NIDs), call detail records (CDRs), mobile phone location data, SMS lists, tax identification numbers (TINs), and passport information.

The report identified 10 active websites and over 600 Facebook advertisements in a single month. Researchers found that NID PDFs were delivered within 17 minutes for a payment of Tk 500.

In another instance, call detail records (CDRs) for a mobile number were provided within two and a half hours after a payment of Tk 1,050, matching the subscriber's actual call history.

Mobile tower-based location data, including a Google Maps link, was also obtained for a payment, delivered within 16 minutes of the payment.

Some sellers claim to use an API to breach government servers to collect this data, though Dismislab could not independently verify this specific claim.

Experts warn that CDRs can be used to track a person's movement patterns and identify who they have been in contact with, posing a significant privacy risk.

headline_marked: Trump expresses hope of [[meeting PM Tarique Rahman soon]]
headline: Trump expresses hope of meeting PM Tarique Rahman soon
summary: US President Donald Trump thanked the Bangladeshi prime minister for purchasing Boeing aircraft and expressed optimism about the country's future.
details: US President Donald Trump has expressed hope of meeting Prime Minister Tarique Rahman soon, stating that Bangladesh and its people have a “very bright future” under his leadership.
In a letter to the Bangladeshi prime minister, Trump voiced optimism about the country's future, noting that Bangladeshis had been through much.
According to the Prime Minister’s Press Wing, Trump conveyed his “warmest regards and love” to the people of Bangladesh.
Trump specifically thanked Tarique Rahman for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft, stating that the company "will not let you down, and I will not forget."
The US president concluded his letter by stating that he looks forward to meeting the Prime Minister in the "not too distant future."
caption:
Donald Trump writes to PM Tarique Rahman, expressing hope for a meeting and thanking him for Boeing aircraft purchase.

US President Donald Trump has expressed hope of meeting Prime Minister Tarique Rahman soon, stating that Bangladesh and its people have a “very bright future” under his leadership.

In a letter to the Bangladeshi prime minister, Trump voiced optimism about the country's future, noting that Bangladeshis had been through much.

According to the Prime Minister’s Press Wing, Trump conveyed his “warmest regards and love” to the people of Bangladesh.

Trump specifically thanked Tarique Rahman for the decision to purchase Boeing aircraft, stating that the company "will not let you down, and I will not forget."

The US president concluded his letter by stating that he looks forward to meeting the Prime Minister in the "not too distant future."

Source: Prothom Alo, Jamuna TV, The Daily Star, Dhaka Tribune
